For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Keyed authenticated wrappers for the plaintext v1 checkpoints and keys.
2	
3	The Lamport (:meth:`pqattest.OneTimeSigner.checkpoint`), W-OTS
4	(:meth:`pqattest.WOTSOneTimeSigner.checkpoint`) and Merkle
5	(:meth:`pqattest.MerkleSigner.checkpoint`) checkpoints all serialise the
6	signing key in the clear and end in a plain SHA-256 checksum that only
7	detects accidental corruption, and the toy lattice private key's versioned
8	encoding (:meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.to_bytes`) is likewise
9	unprotected. :func:`auth_wrap` adds an outer
10	HMAC-SHA-256 envelope so a party holding the shared key can tell whether a
11	checkpoint or lattice key was altered by someone without the key;
12	:func:`auth_unwrap` verifies the tag and hands the original payload bytes
13	back.
14	
15	:func:`auth_state_wrap` / :func:`auth_state_unwrap` are the version 2
16	envelope: the same magic, authentication and v1 parameter rules, plus an
17	8-byte unsigned *generation*. :func:`auth_state_unwrap` can refuse a blob
18	whose generation is below a caller-supplied floor, which lets a trusted
19	monotonic counter detect rollback across unwraps (the floor itself is not
20	stored in the envelope and must live in trusted storage).
21	
22	The floor only orders generations: two different payloads wrapped at the
23	same generation are indistinguishable to it. :func:`auth_state_fingerprint`
24	derives a 32-byte state identity from an authenticated v2 envelope, and
25	:func:`auth_state_unwrap` accepts an optional ``expect_state_id`` so a
26	caller can pin the exact envelope body it last accepted alongside the
27	high-water generation.
28	
29	Both envelopes authenticate but do **not** encrypt (the payload stays
30	readable), and a replay of the exact accepted envelope, or a rollback that
31	also rewinds the trusted floor and identity, remains undetectable.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import hashlib
37	import hmac
38	from typing import Any, Callable
39	
40	__all__ = [
41	    "auth_wrap",
42	    "auth_unwrap",
43	    "auth_state_wrap",
44	    "auth_state_unwrap",
45	    "auth_state_fingerprint",
46	]
47	
48	_AUTH_MAGIC = b"PQAAUTH\0"
49	_AUTH_TAG_BYTES = 32  # HMAC-SHA-256 output length
50	_STATE_ID_BYTES = 32  # HMAC-SHA-256 output length
51	_STATE_ID_DOMAIN = b"pqattest/auth-state-id/v1"
52	_UINT64_MAX = 2**64 - 1
53	
54	# v1 envelope: magic, version, scheme identifier, 4-byte payload length.
55	_AUTH_V1_VERSION = 1
56	_AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 4
57	
58	# v2 envelope: magic, version, scheme identifier, 8-byte generation, 4-byte
59	# payload length.
60	_AUTH_V2_VERSION = 2
61	_AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 8 + 4
62	
63	# Scheme name -> (envelope identifier, magic prefix of the wrapped payload).
64	# The magic bytes match the v1 checkpoint codecs in the lamport, wots and
65	# merkle modules and the v1 private key codec in the toy_lattice module; they
66	# are restated here so this module owns the envelope's
67	# scheme table without importing the package init.
68	_SCHEMES: dict[str, tuple[int, bytes]] = {
69	    "lamport": (1, b"PQALCP\0\0"),
70	    "wots": (2, b"PQAWCP\0\0"),
71	    "merkle": (3, b"PQAMSCP\0"),
72	    "lattice": (4, b"PQALSK\0\0"),
73	}
74	_SCHEME_IDS: dict[int, tuple[str, bytes]] = {
75	    identifier: (name, magic) for name, (identifier, magic) in _SCHEMES.items()
76	}

79	def _coerce_bytes(value: Any, label: str) -> bytes:
80	    if isinstance(value, bytes):
81	        return value
82	    if isinstance(value, bytearray):
83	        return bytes(value)
84	    raise TypeError(f"{label} must be bytes or bytearray")
85	
86	
87	def _validate_key(key: Any) -> bytes:
88	    key_bytes = _coerce_bytes(key, "key")
89	    if not key_bytes:
90	        raise ValueError("key must not be empty")
91	    return key_bytes
92	
93	
94	def _validate_generation(value: Any, label: str) -> int:
95	    """Coerce a keyword argument that must be a non-boolean uint64."""
96	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
97	        raise TypeError(f"{label} must be a non-boolean integer between 0 and 2**64-1")
98	    if not 0 <= value <= _UINT64_MAX:
99	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be between 0 and 2**64-1")
100	    return value
101	
102	
103	def _validate_expect(expect: Any) -> None:
104	    if expect is None:
105	        return
106	    if not isinstance(expect, str):
107	        raise TypeError("expect must be a scheme name string or None")
108	    if expect not in _SCHEMES:
109	        raise ValueError(f"unknown expected scheme: {expect!r}")
110	
111	
112	def _validate_state_id(state_id: Any, label: str) -> bytes | None:
113	    """Coerce an optional 32-byte state identity keyword argument."""
114	    if state_id is None:
115	        return None
116	    state_id_bytes = _coerce_bytes(state_id, label)
117	    if len(state_id_bytes) != _STATE_ID_BYTES:
118	        raise ValueError(
119	            f"{label} must be exactly {_STATE_ID_BYTES} bytes"
120	        )
121	    return state_id_bytes

124	def _state_identity(body: bytes, key_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
125	    """Compute the 32-byte state identity over an authenticated v2 body.
126	
127	    The identity is a domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 under the same key over
128	    the exact body bytes the envelope tag authenticates (everything before
129	    the 32-byte tag), so it binds scheme, generation, length and payload
130	    without reusing the envelope tag directly.
131	    """
132	    return hmac.new(
133	        key_bytes, _STATE_ID_DOMAIN + body, hashlib.sha256
134	    ).digest()

137	def _check_payload_magic(payload: bytes, payload_magic: bytes, scheme: str) -> None:
138	    if len(payload) < len(payload_magic) or payload[: len(payload_magic)] != payload_magic:
139	        raise ValueError("payload magic does not match the envelope scheme")

142	def auth_wrap(checkpoint: Any, *, scheme: Any, key: Any) -> bytes:
143	    """Wrap a plaintext v1 signer checkpoint or lattice key in a keyed authenticated envelope.
144	
145	    ``checkpoint`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` holding the output of
146	    one of the three existing checkpoint serialisers or of
147	    :meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.to_bytes`; ``key`` must be a
148	    non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret; ``scheme`` is
149	    keyword-only and one of ``"lamport"``, ``"wots"``, ``"merkle"`` or
150	    ``"lattice"``.
151	    A non-bytes ``checkpoint``/``key`` or a non-str ``scheme`` raises
152	    ``TypeError``; an empty key, an unknown scheme or a payload whose
153	    magic does not match the named scheme raises ``ValueError``.
154	
155	    The v1 envelope layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAAUTH\\0"``; one byte
156	    each for the version (1) and the scheme identifier (lamport=1, wots=2,
157	    merkle=3, lattice=4); the payload length as 4 big-endian bytes; the
158	    original
159	    payload unchanged; and finally the 32-byte
160	    ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, all preceding bytes)`` tag. Encoding is
161	    deterministic: the same payload, scheme and key always produce the
162	    same bytes. The payload is not encrypted — the envelope only lets a
163	    key holder detect keyless tampering.
164	    """
165	    payload = _coerce_bytes(checkpoint, "checkpoint")
166	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
167	    if not isinstance(scheme, str):
168	        raise TypeError("scheme must be a string")
169	    try:
170	        identifier, payload_magic = _SCHEMES[scheme]
171	    except KeyError:
172	        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}") from None
173	    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
174	    body = (
175	        _AUTH_MAGIC
176	        + bytes((_AUTH_V1_VERSION, identifier))
177	        + len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
178	        + payload
179	    )
180	    return body + hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
181

183	def auth_unwrap(data: Any, *, key: Any, expect: Any = None) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
184	    """Verify a v1 authenticated envelope and return ``(scheme, payload)``.
185	
186	    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
187	    :func:`auth_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared
188	    secret; the keyword-only ``expect`` may name a scheme
189	    (``"lamport"``/``"wots"``/``"merkle"``/``"lattice"``) that the envelope
190	    identifier must then match. Wrong parameter types raise ``TypeError``; an
191	    empty
192	    key, an unknown ``expect`` scheme, a bad envelope magic, version or
193	    scheme identifier, a length field that does not match the content,
194	    truncation, trailing data, a payload magic that does not match its
195	    scheme identifier, an identifier different from ``expect`` or a bad
196	    HMAC tag raises ``ValueError`` and nothing is returned. A v2 envelope
197	    (from :func:`auth_state_wrap`) is rejected as an unsupported version.
198	
199	    The tag is checked with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any payload
200	    byte is trusted; only afterwards is the payload magic checked against
201	    the scheme identifier. The returned payload is the exact bytes
202	    passed to :func:`auth_wrap` (as ``bytes``), ready for the matching
203	    ``from_checkpoint`` (or :meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.from_bytes`
204	    for ``"lattice"``). The envelope authenticates but does not encrypt
205	    and does not prevent copying, replay or rollback of an older valid blob.
206	    """
207	    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
208	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
209	    _validate_expect(expect)
210	
211	    minimum_length = _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + _AUTH_TAG_BYTES
212	    if len(blob) < minimum_length:
213	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
214	    if blob[:8] != _AUTH_MAGIC:
215	        raise ValueError("bad authenticated checkpoint magic")
216	    if blob[8] != _AUTH_V1_VERSION:
217	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported authenticated checkpoint version: {blob[8]}")
218	    identifier = blob[9]
219	    try:
220	        scheme, payload_magic = _SCHEME_IDS[identifier]
221	    except KeyError:
222	        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme identifier: {identifier}") from None
223	    payload_length = int.from_bytes(blob[10:14], "big")
224	    expected_length = _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length + _AUTH_TAG_BYTES
225	    if len(blob) < expected_length:
226	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
227	    if len(blob) > expected_length:
228	        raise ValueError("trailing data after the authenticated checkpoint")
229	
230	    body, tag = blob[:-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES], blob[-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES:]
231	    expected_tag = hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
232	    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_tag, tag):
233	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint tag mismatch")
234	
235	    payload = blob[_AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES : _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length]
236	    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
237	    if expect is not None and scheme != expect:
238	        raise ValueError(f"envelope scheme {scheme!r} does not match expected {expect!r}")
239	    return scheme, bytes(payload)

242	def auth_state_wrap(
243	    checkpoint: Any, *, scheme: Any, key: Any, generation: Any
244	) -> bytes:
245	    """Wrap a checkpoint or lattice key in the version 2 authenticated, generation-tagged envelope.
246	
247	    Behaves exactly like :func:`auth_wrap` — same ``checkpoint``, ``scheme``
248	    and ``key`` constraints and the same payload-magic check — but
249	    additionally binds a keyword-only ``generation``: a non-boolean integer
250	    from ``0`` to ``2**64 - 1`` (a wrong type raises ``TypeError``, an
251	    out-of-range value ``ValueError``).
252	
253	    The v2 envelope layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAAUTH\\0"``; one byte
254	    each for the version (2) and the scheme identifier (lamport=1, wots=2,
255	    merkle=3, lattice=4); the generation as 8 big-endian bytes; the payload
256	    length as
257	    4 big-endian bytes; the original payload unchanged; and
258	    finally the 32-byte ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, all preceding bytes)`` tag.
259	    Encoding is deterministic: identical inputs produce identical bytes.
260	    The payload is not encrypted, and the generation only helps a caller
261	    that tracks a trusted high-water mark — it proves nothing on its own.
262	    """
263	    payload = _coerce_bytes(checkpoint, "checkpoint")
264	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
265	    generation_value = _validate_generation(generation, "generation")
266	    if not isinstance(scheme, str):
267	        raise TypeError("scheme must be a string")
268	    try:
269	        identifier, payload_magic = _SCHEMES[scheme]
270	    except KeyError:
271	        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}") from None
272	    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
273	    body = (
274	        _AUTH_MAGIC
275	        + bytes((_AUTH_V2_VERSION, identifier))
276	        + generation_value.to_bytes(8, "big")
277	        + len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
278	        + payload
279	    )
280	    return body + hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
281	
282	
283	def _auth_state_authenticate(blob: bytes, key_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
284	    """Verify the v2 HMAC tag and return the authenticated body.
285	
286	    Once at least the 32 tag bytes are present, the last 32 bytes are taken
287	    as the tag and everything before them as the authenticated body; the tag
288	    is verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any field is trusted.
289	    """
290	    if len(blob) < _AUTH_TAG_BYTES:
291	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
292	    body, tag = blob[:-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES], blob[-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES:]
293	    expected_tag = hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
294	    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_tag, tag):
295	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint tag mismatch")
296	    return body
297	
298	
299	def _auth_state_parse(
300	    body: bytes, *, expect: Any, min_generation: Any
301	) -> tuple[str, int, bytes]:
302	    """Parse an authenticated v2 body into ``(scheme, generation, payload)``.
303	
304	    Only called on a body whose tag has already verified; checks the magic,
305	    version, scheme identifier, length field, payload magic, ``expect`` and
306	    the generation floor, in that order.
307	    """
308	    if len(body) < _AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES:
309	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
310	    if body[:8] != _AUTH_MAGIC:
311	        raise ValueError("bad authenticated checkpoint magic")
312	    if body[8] != _AUTH_V2_VERSION:
313	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported authenticated checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
314	    identifier = body[9]
315	    try:
316	        scheme, payload_magic = _SCHEME_IDS[identifier]
317	    except KeyError:
318	        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme identifier: {identifier}") from None
319	    generation = int.from_bytes(body[10:18], "big")
320	    payload_length = int.from_bytes(body[18:22], "big")
321	    expected_length = _AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length
322	    if len(body) < expected_length:
323	        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
324	    if len(body) > expected_length:
325	        raise ValueError("trailing data after the authenticated checkpoint")
326	
327	    payload = body[_AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES:expected_length]
328	    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
329	    if expect is not None and scheme != expect:
330	        raise ValueError(f"envelope scheme {scheme!r} does not match expected {expect!r}")
331	    if min_generation is not None and generation < min_generation:
332	        raise ValueError(
333	            f"checkpoint generation {generation} is below the minimum {min_generation}"
334	        )
335	    return scheme, generation, bytes(payload)

338	def auth_state_unwrap(
339	    data: Any, *, key: Any, expect: Any = None, min_generation: Any = None,
340	    expect_state_id: Any = None,
341	) -> tuple[str, int, bytes]:
342	    """Verify a v2 envelope and return ``(scheme, generation, payload)``.
343	
344	    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
345	    :func:`auth_state_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray``
346	    shared secret. ``expect`` may name a scheme the envelope must match.
347	    ``min_generation`` is ``None`` (the default: no floor) or a non-boolean
348	    integer from ``0`` to ``2**64 - 1``; when given, an envelope whose
349	    generation is below the floor is rejected. The floor is *not* carried in
350	    the envelope — persist it in trusted storage, or an attacker who can
351	    roll the checkpoint back and rewind the floor defeats the check.
352	
353	    ``expect_state_id`` is ``None`` (the default) or exactly 32
354	    ``bytes``/``bytearray``, normally the value
355	    :func:`auth_state_fingerprint` returned for the previously accepted
356	    envelope. When given, the envelope's state identity must match it
357	    (compared with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`) or ``ValueError`` is raised;
358	    this distinguishes two different payloads wrapped at the same
359	    generation, which the floor alone cannot. Persist the identity
360	    atomically with the floor, or a rollback that rewinds both is no more
361	    detectable than with the floor alone. When omitted, the return value
362	    and exception semantics are exactly as before.
363	
364	    Wrong parameter types raise ``TypeError`` (a non-bytes
365	    ``data``/``key``/``expect_state_id``, a non-string ``expect``, a
366	    non-integer or boolean ``min_generation``); an empty key, an unknown
367	    ``expect``/floor value out of the uint64 range, an
368	    ``expect_state_id`` whose length is not 32, a bad envelope magic, a
369	    version other than 2 (including a v1 envelope), an unknown scheme
370	    identifier, a mismatched length field, truncation, trailing data, a
371	    bad HMAC tag, a payload magic that does not match its scheme
372	    identifier, an identifier different from ``expect``, a generation
373	    below ``min_generation`` or a state identity different from
374	    ``expect_state_id`` raises ``ValueError``.
375	
376	    Once at least the 32 tag bytes are present, the last 32 bytes are taken
377	    as the tag and everything before them as the authenticated body; the tag
378	    is verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any field is
379	    trusted. Only afterwards are the v2 fields and the payload parsed, the
380	    payload magic and the scheme (including ``expect``) checked, and the
381	    generation floor applied; the state identity is compared last, after
382	    the tag and every existing condition have passed. The returned
383	    checkpoint is the exact payload passed to :func:`auth_state_wrap` (as
384	    ``bytes``), ready for the matching ``from_checkpoint``. The envelope
385	    authenticates but does not encrypt; a replay of the exact accepted
386	    envelope, or a rollback accompanied by a floor and identity rewind,
387	    remains undetectable.
388	    """
389	    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
390	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
391	    _validate_expect(expect)
392	    if min_generation is not None:
393	        _validate_generation(min_generation, "min_generation")
394	    expected_state_id = _validate_state_id(expect_state_id, "expect_state_id")
395	
396	    # Authenticate first: no field (including the generation) is trusted
397	    # until this tag over the whole body checks out.
398	    body = _auth_state_authenticate(blob, key_bytes)
399	    result = _auth_state_parse(body, expect=expect, min_generation=min_generation)
400	    if expected_state_id is not None:
401	        # Only compared once the tag and every pre-existing condition have
402	        # passed, so no field of an unauthenticated blob ever reaches this
403	        # check; the comparison itself is constant time.
404	        actual_state_id = _state_identity(body, key_bytes)
405	        if not hmac.compare_digest(actual_state_id, expected_state_id):
406	            raise ValueError("checkpoint state identity does not match expect_state_id")
407	    return result
408

410	def auth_state_fingerprint(data: Any, *, key: Any) -> bytes:
411	    """Return the 32-byte state identity of an authenticated v2 envelope.
412	
413	    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
414	    :func:`auth_state_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray``
415	    shared secret. The envelope's existing HMAC tag is verified first with
416	    :func:`hmac.compare_digest` exactly as in :func:`auth_state_unwrap`,
417	    and the envelope must then parse as a well-formed v2 blob (correct
418	    magic, version 2, known scheme identifier, matching length field, no
419	    truncation or trailing data, payload magic matching the scheme
420	    identifier); only then is the identity computed as
421	    ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, b"pqattest/auth-state-id/v1" + body)`` over the
422	    exact authenticated v2 body (all bytes before the 32-byte tag). The
423	    result is always 32 ``bytes`` and deterministic: the same envelope and
424	    key always return the same value, while any difference in payload,
425	    generation, scheme identifier or key yields a different identity.
426	
427	    The identity binds the authenticated body but is not a secret from a
428	    party holding the envelope, and it does not encrypt the payload; save
429	    it in trusted storage and pass it as ``expect_state_id`` to
430	    :func:`auth_state_unwrap` to reject a different state at the same
431	    generation. A non-bytes ``data``/``key`` raises ``TypeError``; an empty
432	    key, a bad HMAC tag, a bad magic or a version other than 2 (including
433	    a v1 envelope), an unknown scheme identifier, a mismatched length
434	    field, truncation, trailing data or a payload magic that does not
435	    match the scheme identifier raises ``ValueError``.
436	    """
437	    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
438	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
439	    # Authenticate first, then enforce the v2 shape: a v1 envelope carries
440	    # a valid HMAC tag under the same key but has no state identity.
441	    body = _auth_state_authenticate(blob, key_bytes)
442	    _auth_state_parse(body, expect=None, min_generation=None)
443	    return _state_identity(body, key_bytes)
444

446	def _validate_claim(claim: Any) -> Callable[..., Any]:
447	    if not callable(claim):
448	        raise TypeError("claim must be callable")
449	    return claim

452	def _restore_auth_state(scheme: str, data: Any, *, key: Any, min_generation: Any,
453	                        claim: Any, restore: Callable[[bytes], Any]) -> tuple[Any, int]:
454	    """Validate, authenticate and restore one v2 envelope, then claim it once.
455	
456	    Shared implementation behind the one-time signers' ``from_auth_state``.
457	    Argument types are checked first, the v2 HMAC tag is verified with
458	    :func:`hmac.compare_digest`, the envelope is fixed to ``scheme`` and the
459	    generation floor applied, and only then is the untouched payload handed to
460	    ``restore``; the ``claim`` callback is invoked exactly once, after the
461	    restore has fully succeeded, and its return value is accepted only when it
462	    ``is True``. Any exception raised by ``claim`` propagates untouched.
463	    """
464	    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
465	        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
466	    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
467	    if min_generation is not None:
468	        _validate_generation(min_generation, "min_generation")
469	    claim_callable = _validate_claim(claim)
470	    _, generation_value, checkpoint = auth_state_unwrap(

"""Keyed authenticated wrappers for the plaintext v1 checkpoints and keys.

The Lamport (:meth:`pqattest.OneTimeSigner.checkpoint`), W-OTS
(:meth:`pqattest.WOTSOneTimeSigner.checkpoint`) and Merkle
(:meth:`pqattest.MerkleSigner.checkpoint`) checkpoints all serialise the
signing key in the clear and end in a plain SHA-256 checksum that only
detects accidental corruption, and the toy lattice private key's versioned
encoding (:meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.to_bytes`) is likewise
unprotected. :func:`auth_wrap` adds an outer
HMAC-SHA-256 envelope so a party holding the shared key can tell whether a
checkpoint or lattice key was altered by someone without the key;
:func:`auth_unwrap` verifies the tag and hands the original payload bytes
back.

:func:`auth_state_wrap` / :func:`auth_state_unwrap` are the version 2
envelope: the same magic, authentication and v1 parameter rules, plus an
8-byte unsigned *generation*. :func:`auth_state_unwrap` can refuse a blob
whose generation is below a caller-supplied floor, which lets a trusted
monotonic counter detect rollback across unwraps (the floor itself is not
stored in the envelope and must live in trusted storage).

The floor only orders generations: two different payloads wrapped at the
same generation are indistinguishable to it. :func:`auth_state_fingerprint`
derives a 32-byte state identity from an authenticated v2 envelope, and
:func:`auth_state_unwrap` accepts an optional ``expect_state_id`` so a
caller can pin the exact envelope body it last accepted alongside the
high-water generation.

Both envelopes authenticate but do **not** encrypt (the payload stays
readable), and a replay of the exact accepted envelope, or a rollback that
also rewinds the trusted floor and identity, remains undetectable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
from typing import Any, Callable

__all__ = [
    "auth_wrap",
    "auth_unwrap",
    "auth_state_wrap",
    "auth_state_unwrap",
    "auth_state_fingerprint",
]

_AUTH_MAGIC = b"PQAAUTH\0"
_AUTH_TAG_BYTES = 32  # HMAC-SHA-256 output length
_STATE_ID_BYTES = 32  # HMAC-SHA-256 output length
_STATE_ID_DOMAIN = b"pqattest/auth-state-id/v1"
_UINT64_MAX = 2**64 - 1

# v1 envelope: magic, version, scheme identifier, 4-byte payload length.
_AUTH_V1_VERSION = 1
_AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 4

# v2 envelope: magic, version, scheme identifier, 8-byte generation, 4-byte
# payload length.
_AUTH_V2_VERSION = 2
_AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 8 + 4

# Scheme name -> (envelope identifier, magic prefix of the wrapped payload).
# The magic bytes match the v1 checkpoint codecs in the lamport, wots and
# merkle modules and the v1 private key codec in the toy_lattice module; they
# are restated here so this module owns the envelope's
# scheme table without importing the package init.
_SCHEMES: dict[str, tuple[int, bytes]] = {
    "lamport": (1, b"PQALCP\0\0"),
    "wots": (2, b"PQAWCP\0\0"),
    "merkle": (3, b"PQAMSCP\0"),
    "lattice": (4, b"PQALSK\0\0"),
}
_SCHEME_IDS: dict[int, tuple[str, bytes]] = {
    identifier: (name, magic) for name, (identifier, magic) in _SCHEMES.items()
}


def _coerce_bytes(value: Any, label: str) -> bytes:
    if isinstance(value, bytes):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, bytearray):
        return bytes(value)
    raise TypeError(f"{label} must be bytes or bytearray")


def _validate_key(key: Any) -> bytes:
    key_bytes = _coerce_bytes(key, "key")
    if not key_bytes:
        raise ValueError("key must not be empty")
    return key_bytes


def _validate_generation(value: Any, label: str) -> int:
    """Coerce a keyword argument that must be a non-boolean uint64."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise TypeError(f"{label} must be a non-boolean integer between 0 and 2**64-1")
    if not 0 <= value <= _UINT64_MAX:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be between 0 and 2**64-1")
    return value


def _validate_expect(expect: Any) -> None:
    if expect is None:
        return
    if not isinstance(expect, str):
        raise TypeError("expect must be a scheme name string or None")
    if expect not in _SCHEMES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown expected scheme: {expect!r}")


def _validate_state_id(state_id: Any, label: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Coerce an optional 32-byte state identity keyword argument."""
    if state_id is None:
        return None
    state_id_bytes = _coerce_bytes(state_id, label)
    if len(state_id_bytes) != _STATE_ID_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} must be exactly {_STATE_ID_BYTES} bytes"
        )
    return state_id_bytes


def _state_identity(body: bytes, key_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Compute the 32-byte state identity over an authenticated v2 body.

    The identity is a domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 under the same key over
    the exact body bytes the envelope tag authenticates (everything before
    the 32-byte tag), so it binds scheme, generation, length and payload
    without reusing the envelope tag directly.
    """
    return hmac.new(
        key_bytes, _STATE_ID_DOMAIN + body, hashlib.sha256
    ).digest()


def _check_payload_magic(payload: bytes, payload_magic: bytes, scheme: str) -> None:
    if len(payload) < len(payload_magic) or payload[: len(payload_magic)] != payload_magic:
        raise ValueError("payload magic does not match the envelope scheme")


def auth_wrap(checkpoint: Any, *, scheme: Any, key: Any) -> bytes:
    """Wrap a plaintext v1 signer checkpoint or lattice key in a keyed authenticated envelope.

    ``checkpoint`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` holding the output of
    one of the three existing checkpoint serialisers or of
    :meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.to_bytes`; ``key`` must be a
    non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret; ``scheme`` is
    keyword-only and one of ``"lamport"``, ``"wots"``, ``"merkle"`` or
    ``"lattice"``.
    A non-bytes ``checkpoint``/``key`` or a non-str ``scheme`` raises
    ``TypeError``; an empty key, an unknown scheme or a payload whose
    magic does not match the named scheme raises ``ValueError``.

    The v1 envelope layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAAUTH\\0"``; one byte
    each for the version (1) and the scheme identifier (lamport=1, wots=2,
    merkle=3, lattice=4); the payload length as 4 big-endian bytes; the
    original
    payload unchanged; and finally the 32-byte
    ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, all preceding bytes)`` tag. Encoding is
    deterministic: the same payload, scheme and key always produce the
    same bytes. The payload is not encrypted — the envelope only lets a
    key holder detect keyless tampering.
    """
    payload = _coerce_bytes(checkpoint, "checkpoint")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    if not isinstance(scheme, str):
        raise TypeError("scheme must be a string")
    try:
        identifier, payload_magic = _SCHEMES[scheme]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}") from None
    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
    body = (
        _AUTH_MAGIC
        + bytes((_AUTH_V1_VERSION, identifier))
        + len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
        + payload
    )
    return body + hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()


def auth_unwrap(data: Any, *, key: Any, expect: Any = None) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    """Verify a v1 authenticated envelope and return ``(scheme, payload)``.

    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
    :func:`auth_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared
    secret; the keyword-only ``expect`` may name a scheme
    (``"lamport"``/``"wots"``/``"merkle"``/``"lattice"``) that the envelope
    identifier must then match. Wrong parameter types raise ``TypeError``; an
    empty
    key, an unknown ``expect`` scheme, a bad envelope magic, version or
    scheme identifier, a length field that does not match the content,
    truncation, trailing data, a payload magic that does not match its
    scheme identifier, an identifier different from ``expect`` or a bad
    HMAC tag raises ``ValueError`` and nothing is returned. A v2 envelope
    (from :func:`auth_state_wrap`) is rejected as an unsupported version.

    The tag is checked with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any payload
    byte is trusted; only afterwards is the payload magic checked against
    the scheme identifier. The returned payload is the exact bytes
    passed to :func:`auth_wrap` (as ``bytes``), ready for the matching
    ``from_checkpoint`` (or :meth:`pqattest.ToyLatticePrivateKey.from_bytes`
    for ``"lattice"``). The envelope authenticates but does not encrypt
    and does not prevent copying, replay or rollback of an older valid blob.
    """
    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    _validate_expect(expect)

    minimum_length = _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + _AUTH_TAG_BYTES
    if len(blob) < minimum_length:
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
    if blob[:8] != _AUTH_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError("bad authenticated checkpoint magic")
    if blob[8] != _AUTH_V1_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported authenticated checkpoint version: {blob[8]}")
    identifier = blob[9]
    try:
        scheme, payload_magic = _SCHEME_IDS[identifier]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme identifier: {identifier}") from None
    payload_length = int.from_bytes(blob[10:14], "big")
    expected_length = _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length + _AUTH_TAG_BYTES
    if len(blob) < expected_length:
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
    if len(blob) > expected_length:
        raise ValueError("trailing data after the authenticated checkpoint")

    body, tag = blob[:-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES], blob[-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES:]
    expected_tag = hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_tag, tag):
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint tag mismatch")

    payload = blob[_AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES : _AUTH_V1_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length]
    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
    if expect is not None and scheme != expect:
        raise ValueError(f"envelope scheme {scheme!r} does not match expected {expect!r}")
    return scheme, bytes(payload)


def auth_state_wrap(
    checkpoint: Any, *, scheme: Any, key: Any, generation: Any
) -> bytes:
    """Wrap a checkpoint or lattice key in the version 2 authenticated, generation-tagged envelope.

    Behaves exactly like :func:`auth_wrap` — same ``checkpoint``, ``scheme``
    and ``key`` constraints and the same payload-magic check — but
    additionally binds a keyword-only ``generation``: a non-boolean integer
    from ``0`` to ``2**64 - 1`` (a wrong type raises ``TypeError``, an
    out-of-range value ``ValueError``).

    The v2 envelope layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAAUTH\\0"``; one byte
    each for the version (2) and the scheme identifier (lamport=1, wots=2,
    merkle=3, lattice=4); the generation as 8 big-endian bytes; the payload
    length as
    4 big-endian bytes; the original payload unchanged; and
    finally the 32-byte ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, all preceding bytes)`` tag.
    Encoding is deterministic: identical inputs produce identical bytes.
    The payload is not encrypted, and the generation only helps a caller
    that tracks a trusted high-water mark — it proves nothing on its own.
    """
    payload = _coerce_bytes(checkpoint, "checkpoint")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    generation_value = _validate_generation(generation, "generation")
    if not isinstance(scheme, str):
        raise TypeError("scheme must be a string")
    try:
        identifier, payload_magic = _SCHEMES[scheme]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}") from None
    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
    body = (
        _AUTH_MAGIC
        + bytes((_AUTH_V2_VERSION, identifier))
        + generation_value.to_bytes(8, "big")
        + len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
        + payload
    )
    return body + hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()


def _auth_state_authenticate(blob: bytes, key_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Verify the v2 HMAC tag and return the authenticated body.

    Once at least the 32 tag bytes are present, the last 32 bytes are taken
    as the tag and everything before them as the authenticated body; the tag
    is verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any field is trusted.
    """
    if len(blob) < _AUTH_TAG_BYTES:
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
    body, tag = blob[:-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES], blob[-_AUTH_TAG_BYTES:]
    expected_tag = hmac.new(key_bytes, body, hashlib.sha256).digest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_tag, tag):
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint tag mismatch")
    return body


def _auth_state_parse(
    body: bytes, *, expect: Any, min_generation: Any
) -> tuple[str, int, bytes]:
    """Parse an authenticated v2 body into ``(scheme, generation, payload)``.

    Only called on a body whose tag has already verified; checks the magic,
    version, scheme identifier, length field, payload magic, ``expect`` and
    the generation floor, in that order.
    """
    if len(body) < _AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES:
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
    if body[:8] != _AUTH_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError("bad authenticated checkpoint magic")
    if body[8] != _AUTH_V2_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported authenticated checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
    identifier = body[9]
    try:
        scheme, payload_magic = _SCHEME_IDS[identifier]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme identifier: {identifier}") from None
    generation = int.from_bytes(body[10:18], "big")
    payload_length = int.from_bytes(body[18:22], "big")
    expected_length = _AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES + payload_length
    if len(body) < expected_length:
        raise ValueError("authenticated checkpoint is truncated")
    if len(body) > expected_length:
        raise ValueError("trailing data after the authenticated checkpoint")

    payload = body[_AUTH_V2_HEADER_BYTES:expected_length]
    _check_payload_magic(payload, payload_magic, scheme)
    if expect is not None and scheme != expect:
        raise ValueError(f"envelope scheme {scheme!r} does not match expected {expect!r}")
    if min_generation is not None and generation < min_generation:
        raise ValueError(
            f"checkpoint generation {generation} is below the minimum {min_generation}"
        )
    return scheme, generation, bytes(payload)


def auth_state_unwrap(
    data: Any, *, key: Any, expect: Any = None, min_generation: Any = None,
    expect_state_id: Any = None,
) -> tuple[str, int, bytes]:
    """Verify a v2 envelope and return ``(scheme, generation, payload)``.

    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
    :func:`auth_state_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray``
    shared secret. ``expect`` may name a scheme the envelope must match.
    ``min_generation`` is ``None`` (the default: no floor) or a non-boolean
    integer from ``0`` to ``2**64 - 1``; when given, an envelope whose
    generation is below the floor is rejected. The floor is *not* carried in
    the envelope — persist it in trusted storage, or an attacker who can
    roll the checkpoint back and rewind the floor defeats the check.

    ``expect_state_id`` is ``None`` (the default) or exactly 32
    ``bytes``/``bytearray``, normally the value
    :func:`auth_state_fingerprint` returned for the previously accepted
    envelope. When given, the envelope's state identity must match it
    (compared with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`) or ``ValueError`` is raised;
    this distinguishes two different payloads wrapped at the same
    generation, which the floor alone cannot. Persist the identity
    atomically with the floor, or a rollback that rewinds both is no more
    detectable than with the floor alone. When omitted, the return value
    and exception semantics are exactly as before.

    Wrong parameter types raise ``TypeError`` (a non-bytes
    ``data``/``key``/``expect_state_id``, a non-string ``expect``, a
    non-integer or boolean ``min_generation``); an empty key, an unknown
    ``expect``/floor value out of the uint64 range, an
    ``expect_state_id`` whose length is not 32, a bad envelope magic, a
    version other than 2 (including a v1 envelope), an unknown scheme
    identifier, a mismatched length field, truncation, trailing data, a
    bad HMAC tag, a payload magic that does not match its scheme
    identifier, an identifier different from ``expect``, a generation
    below ``min_generation`` or a state identity different from
    ``expect_state_id`` raises ``ValueError``.

    Once at least the 32 tag bytes are present, the last 32 bytes are taken
    as the tag and everything before them as the authenticated body; the tag
    is verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before any field is
    trusted. Only afterwards are the v2 fields and the payload parsed, the
    payload magic and the scheme (including ``expect``) checked, and the
    generation floor applied; the state identity is compared last, after
    the tag and every existing condition have passed. The returned
    checkpoint is the exact payload passed to :func:`auth_state_wrap` (as
    ``bytes``), ready for the matching ``from_checkpoint``. The envelope
    authenticates but does not encrypt; a replay of the exact accepted
    envelope, or a rollback accompanied by a floor and identity rewind,
    remains undetectable.
    """
    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    _validate_expect(expect)
    if min_generation is not None:
        _validate_generation(min_generation, "min_generation")
    expected_state_id = _validate_state_id(expect_state_id, "expect_state_id")

    # Authenticate first: no field (including the generation) is trusted
    # until this tag over the whole body checks out.
    body = _auth_state_authenticate(blob, key_bytes)
    result = _auth_state_parse(body, expect=expect, min_generation=min_generation)
    if expected_state_id is not None:
        # Only compared once the tag and every pre-existing condition have
        # passed, so no field of an unauthenticated blob ever reaches this
        # check; the comparison itself is constant time.
        actual_state_id = _state_identity(body, key_bytes)
        if not hmac.compare_digest(actual_state_id, expected_state_id):
            raise ValueError("checkpoint state identity does not match expect_state_id")
    return result


def auth_state_fingerprint(data: Any, *, key: Any) -> bytes:
    """Return the 32-byte state identity of an authenticated v2 envelope.

    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray`` produced by
    :func:`auth_state_wrap` and ``key`` a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray``
    shared secret. The envelope's existing HMAC tag is verified first with
    :func:`hmac.compare_digest` exactly as in :func:`auth_state_unwrap`,
    and the envelope must then parse as a well-formed v2 blob (correct
    magic, version 2, known scheme identifier, matching length field, no
    truncation or trailing data, payload magic matching the scheme
    identifier); only then is the identity computed as
    ``HMAC-SHA-256(key, b"pqattest/auth-state-id/v1" + body)`` over the
    exact authenticated v2 body (all bytes before the 32-byte tag). The
    result is always 32 ``bytes`` and deterministic: the same envelope and
    key always return the same value, while any difference in payload,
    generation, scheme identifier or key yields a different identity.

    The identity binds the authenticated body but is not a secret from a
    party holding the envelope, and it does not encrypt the payload; save
    it in trusted storage and pass it as ``expect_state_id`` to
    :func:`auth_state_unwrap` to reject a different state at the same
    generation. A non-bytes ``data``/``key`` raises ``TypeError``; an empty
    key, a bad HMAC tag, a bad magic or a version other than 2 (including
    a v1 envelope), an unknown scheme identifier, a mismatched length
    field, truncation, trailing data or a payload magic that does not
    match the scheme identifier raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    blob = _coerce_bytes(data, "data")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    # Authenticate first, then enforce the v2 shape: a v1 envelope carries
    # a valid HMAC tag under the same key but has no state identity.
    body = _auth_state_authenticate(blob, key_bytes)
    _auth_state_parse(body, expect=None, min_generation=None)
    return _state_identity(body, key_bytes)


def _validate_claim(claim: Any) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    if not callable(claim):
        raise TypeError("claim must be callable")
    return claim


def _restore_auth_state(scheme: str, data: Any, *, key: Any, min_generation: Any,
                        claim: Any, restore: Callable[[bytes], Any]) -> tuple[Any, int]:
    """Validate, authenticate and restore one v2 envelope, then claim it once.

    Shared implementation behind the one-time signers' ``from_auth_state``.
    Argument types are checked first, the v2 HMAC tag is verified with
    :func:`hmac.compare_digest`, the envelope is fixed to ``scheme`` and the
    generation floor applied, and only then is the untouched payload handed to
    ``restore``; the ``claim`` callback is invoked exactly once, after the
    restore has fully succeeded, and its return value is accepted only when it
    ``is True``. Any exception raised by ``claim`` propagates untouched.
    """
    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    if min_generation is not None:
        _validate_generation(min_generation, "min_generation")
    claim_callable = _validate_claim(claim)
    _, generation_value, checkpoint = auth_state_unwrap(
        data,
        key=key_bytes,
        expect=scheme,
        min_generation=min_generation,
    )
    signer = restore(checkpoint)
    result = claim_callable((scheme, generation_value))
    if result is not True:
        raise ValueError("claim callback did not return True")
    return signer, generation_value


def _restore_auth_state_pair(data_a: Any, data_b: Any, *, key: Any, floor: Any,
                             claim: Any,
                             restore_a: Callable[[bytes], Any],
                             restore_b: Callable[[bytes], Any]
                             ) -> tuple[tuple[Any, Any], int]:
    """Authenticate and restore two same-generation envelopes, then claim both.

    Both blobs must verify under ``key``, the first must be a ``"lamport"``
    envelope and the second a ``"wots"`` envelope, their generations must be
    equal and — when ``floor`` is given — at least that high. Both HMAC tags
    are verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before a single field of
    either envelope is parsed, and both checkpoints are restored before the
    single paired claim, so a caller can never successfully claim only one
    side. ``claim`` is invoked exactly once with
    ``(("lamport", g), ("wots", g))`` after every restore has succeeded, and
    its return value is accepted only when it ``is True``; any exception it
    raises propagates untouched.
    """
    if not isinstance(data_a, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
    if not isinstance(data_b, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    if floor is not None:
        _validate_generation(floor, "floor")
    claim_callable = _validate_claim(claim)
    # Authenticate both sides first: no field of either envelope is trusted
    # until both tags check out.
    body_a = _auth_state_authenticate(bytes(data_a), key_bytes)
    body_b = _auth_state_authenticate(bytes(data_b), key_bytes)
    _, generation_a, checkpoint_a = _auth_state_parse(
        body_a, expect="lamport", min_generation=floor
    )
    _, generation_b, checkpoint_b = _auth_state_parse(
        body_b, expect="wots", min_generation=floor
    )
    if generation_a != generation_b:
        raise ValueError(
            f"lamport generation {generation_a} does not match wots generation {generation_b}"
        )
    signer_a = restore_a(checkpoint_a)
    signer_b = restore_b(checkpoint_b)
    result = claim_callable((("lamport", generation_a), ("wots", generation_b)))
    if result is not True:
        raise ValueError("claim callback did not return True")
    return (signer_a, signer_b), generation_a


def _authenticate_auth_state_pair(
    data_a: Any, data_b: Any, *, key: Any, floor: Any
) -> tuple[int, bytes, bytes]:
    """Authenticate two v2 envelopes and return ``(generation, checkpoint_a, checkpoint_b)``.

    Authentication-only counterpart of :func:`_restore_auth_state_pair` for
    the stateless pair conversion: argument types are checked first, both
    HMAC tags are verified with :func:`hmac.compare_digest` before a single
    field of either envelope is parsed, the first envelope is then fixed to
    ``"lamport"`` and the second to ``"wots"`` (each with its payload magic
    and the generation floor applied), and their generations are required to
    be equal. No checkpoint is restored and no claim is performed here: the
    caller builds every output first and runs the single paired claim only
    afterwards.
    """
    if not isinstance(data_a, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
    if not isinstance(data_b, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError("data must be bytes or bytearray")
    key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
    if floor is not None:
        _validate_generation(floor, "floor")
    # Authenticate both sides first: no field of either envelope is trusted
    # until both tags check out.
    body_a = _auth_state_authenticate(bytes(data_a), key_bytes)
    body_b = _auth_state_authenticate(bytes(data_b), key_bytes)
    _, generation_a, checkpoint_a = _auth_state_parse(
        body_a, expect="lamport", min_generation=floor
    )
    _, generation_b, checkpoint_b = _auth_state_parse(
        body_b, expect="wots", min_generation=floor
    )
    if generation_a != generation_b:
        raise ValueError(
            f"lamport generation {generation_a} does not match wots generation {generation_b}"
        )
    return generation_a, checkpoint_a, checkpoint_b

1	"""Fixed-byte compatibility regression tests for the Lamport v1 formats.
2	
3	These tests pin the on-disk v1 encodings of :class:`PrivateKey`,
4	:class:`PublicKey`, a stateless signature and the :class:`OneTimeSigner`
5	checkpoint to checked-in golden bytes (see
6	``tests/fixtures/lamport_compat/README.md``). The golden samples were
7	produced once from documented deterministic inputs and are only ever
8	read here: they are never regenerated through the encoder under test,
9	and the assertions are byte-for-byte comparisons against the samples
10	rather than length checks or current-version round trips.
11	
12	Coverage for each of ``bits=7`` and ``bits=256``:
13	
14	* a key pair generated through the public ``keygen`` entry from the
15	  documented deterministic ``token_bytes`` input encodes to the frozen
16	  private-key and public-key bytes, and the frozen bytes decode back
17	  through the public decode entries to value-equal keys;
18	* the frozen context-free signature decodes through
19	  ``lamport_signature_from_bytes`` to the same elements a fresh
20	  stateless ``sign`` produces and verifies against the frozen public
21	  key;
22	* restoring the frozen unused checkpoint through
23	  ``OneTimeSigner.from_checkpoint`` gives an unused signer whose first
24	  signature matches the frozen signature and whose post-sign checkpoint
25	  matches the frozen used checkpoint, and ``sign_with_checkpoint`` from
26	  the same initial state returns those same two results;
27	* omitting ``context``, passing ``None`` or passing an empty byte
28	  string all yield the frozen signature bytes, with a separately
29	  restored signer for every comparison;
30	* restoring the frozen used checkpoint gives a signer whose every
31	  ``sign`` raises ``KeyExhaustedError`` and whose checkpoint bytes stay
32	  unchanged.
33	
34	The 256-bit sample additionally proves the frozen signature does not
35	verify for a fixed, different-digest message.
36	
37	The failure cases pin the documented parsing boundaries of every decode
38	entry involved here (``PrivateKey.from_bytes``,
39	``PublicKey.from_bytes``, ``lamport_signature_from_bytes`` and
40	``OneTimeSigner.from_checkpoint``): ``bytes`` and ``bytearray`` are
41	equivalent, a ``str`` raises ``TypeError``, and bad magic / unknown
42	version / truncation / trailing data all raise ``ValueError``. The
43	checkpoint cases additionally cover an invalid ``used`` flag, a wrong
44	key-length field and a checksum mismatch, and corrupt structural fields
45	with a *recomputed* checksum so each field check is proven to fire on
46	its own rather than being masked by the checksum layer.
47	
48	The three test classes separate the three regression signals: encoding
49	byte changes (:class:`LamportCompatVectorTest`), exhausted-state
50	distortion (:class:`LamportCompatExhaustedStateTest`) and old-sample
51	parse failures (:class:`LamportCompatParsingBoundaryTest`).
52	"""
53	
54	import hashlib
55	import os
56	import unittest
57	
58	from pqattest import (
59	    KeyExhaustedError,
60	    OneTimeSigner,
61	    PrivateKey,
62	    PublicKey,
63	    keygen,
64	    lamport_signature_from_bytes,
65	    lamport_signature_to_bytes,
66	    sign,
67	    verify,
68	)
69	
70	FIXTURE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "fixtures", "lamport_compat")
71	
72	MESSAGE = b"compat-lamport-v1"
73	# A fixed, different message; no signature was ever made over it. Used
74	# only on the verifier side, and only meaningfully at 256 bits: at
75	# 7 bits two distinct digests can trivially share their first bits.
76	MESSAGE_TAMPERED = b"compat-lamport-v1-changed"
77	
78	SAMPLE_NAMES = (
79	    "private_key.bin",
80	    "public_key.bin",
81	    "signature.bin",
82	    "checkpoint_unused.bin",
83	    "checkpoint_used.bin",
84	)
85	
86	# Documented v1 codec layout (see the to_bytes docstrings and README):
87	# 8 magic | 1 version | 2 bits | 2 element_count | ...elements...
88	_CODEC_VERSION_OFFSET = 8
89	_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES = 13
90	
91	# Documented v1 checkpoint layout (see OneTimeSigner.checkpoint
92	# docstring and README): 8 magic | 1 version | 1 used |
93	# 4 private-key length | ...private key encoding... | 32 SHA-256.
94	_CHECKPOINT_VERSION_OFFSET = 8
95	_CHECKPOINT_USED_OFFSET = 9
96	_CHECKPOINT_KEY_LENGTH_OFFSET = 10
97	_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES = 32
98	
99	
100	def compat_tokens():
101	    """Deterministic key input shared by the frozen samples.
102	
103	    The first call returns the integer 1 as a 32-byte big-endian value
104	    and every later call the next integer, so every Lamport secret is a
105	    public, repeatable value. Each bit count uses its own independent
106	    counter.
107	    """
108	    state = {"value": 0}
109	
110	    def token_bytes(size: int) -> bytes:
111	        state["value"] += 1
112	        return state["value"].to_bytes(32, "big")
113	
114	    return token_bytes
115	
116	
117	def fixture(bits: int, name: str) -> bytes:
118	    """Read one frozen sample; a missing sample fails, never skips.
119	
120	    A missing golden file is a compatibility failure in its own right
121	    (the fixed regression basis is gone), so it raises
122	    ``AssertionError`` instead of returning ``None`` or triggering
123	    regeneration.
124	    """
125	    path = os.path.join(FIXTURE_DIR, f"b{bits}", name)
126	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
127	        raise AssertionError(
128	            f"missing frozen Lamport compatibility sample: {path!s}; "
129	            "the golden samples must be checked in and must never be "
130	            "regenerated by the test suite"
131	        )
132	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
133	        return handle.read()
134	
135	
136	def load_samples(bits: int) -> dict:
137	    return {
138	        "private_key": fixture(bits, "private_key.bin"),
139	        "public_key": fixture(bits, "public_key.bin"),
140	        "signature": fixture(bits, "signature.bin"),
141	        "checkpoint_unused": fixture(bits, "checkpoint_unused.bin"),
142	        "checkpoint_used": fixture(bits, "checkpoint_used.bin"),
143	    }
144	
145	
146	def decode_entries(samples: dict):
147	    """Every decode entry involved in this chain, with a valid sample."""
148	    return (
149	        ("private_key", PrivateKey.from_bytes, samples["private_key"]),
150	        ("public_key", PublicKey.from_bytes, samples["public_key"]),
151	        ("signature", lamport_signature_from_bytes, samples["signature"]),
152	        (
153	            "checkpoint",
154	            OneTimeSigner.from_checkpoint,
155	            samples["checkpoint_unused"],
156	        ),
157	    )
158	
159	
160	def recompute_checksum(blob: bytes) -> bytes:
161	    """Re-stamp a tampered checkpoint body with a valid SHA-256 checksum."""
162	    body = blob[:-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES]
163	    return body + hashlib.sha256(body).digest()

166	class LamportCompatVectorTest(unittest.TestCase):
167	    def test_all_frozen_samples_are_present(self):

236	        for bits in (7, 256):

309	    def test_restored_used_checkpoint_cannot_sign_and_keeps_bytes(self):

340	    def test_bytes_and_bytearray_decode_equivalently(self):

406	            bad_magic = bytearray(raw)

409	
410	            bad_version = bytearray(raw)

412	            cases["unknown_version"] = bytes(bad_version)

417	
418	            bad_length = bytearray(raw)

442	    def test_checkpoint_checksum_corruption_is_rejected(self):
443	        for bits in (7, 256):
